analysis.title: Thoughts from Q3/26 On-Quarter Software Earnings: Bifurcation continues with a generally disappointing Q3
key_insights: Across 55 on-quarter software companies, the mean Q3/26 revenue beat was 2.5% vs 2.6% in Q2/26, and the mean Q4/26 revenue guide was 1.0% above consensus. Beat levels remain below 2025 levels.
ARR/billings beat consensus by 1.5% on average vs 3.4% in Q2/26, the lowest since Q1/25. Back Office and Front Office missed on ARR/billings, while Vertical and Security had the biggest beats.

Mean profitability beat was 23.0%. Q4/26 profitability guidance moved down about 14% vs consensus because guides likely assume in-quarter beats flow through. CY/26 guidance was up 1.2% for revenue and 4.8% for profitability vs consensus.

Average one-day post-earnings return was -2.3% and average return from earnings to 11/13 was -2.1%. Expectations were elevated into the season and investors looking to widen exposure to tier 2 AI beneficiaries were generally not rewarded.

RBC sees AI crowding out other software spending, taking budget or delaying decisions. DT, HUBS, NOW and TEAM all made macro comments, and NOW and TEAM are rolling out forward-deployed engineer motions to help implement AI. RBC is not banking on a typical Q4 budget flush, though it could be upside.

RBC sees a better setup for the off-quarter cohort after the recent selloff, kicking off with PANW on Wednesday. Its checks were bullish for cyber, with resellers incrementally more optimistic, and it likes tier 1 software AI winners at current valuations.

Investor patience is thin on qualitative AI metrics that do not show up in top-line results. Companies must show AI is driving an upward inflection. A reversion to crowding into tier 1 AI names is possible.
Post-print volatility skewed to the downside vs Q2. FROG, APP, LFTO, MGNI and PCOR rose more than 20%, while FFIV, FTNT, COUR, FSLY, NOW and APPS fell more than 20%.
By subsector, Ad-Tech, Observability and Vertical had the biggest revenue beats, while SaaS and Front Office had the smallest. Ad-Tech rose 13.8% on day one, while Observability fell 14.6%.
The RBC All SaaS index traded at 5.9x FTM EV/S a week before earnings (10/16) vs 5.7x on 11/13, so multiples compressed only modestly.

Reported themes across infra, data and cyber include AI monetization becoming real, agentic AI governance, budgets restructured around AI, longer deal cycles, a shift to consumption and hybrid pricing, rising memory costs hurting hardware-exposed software, and robust US federal spending.

RBC is more positive on AKAM, BSY, DBX, DDOG, FROG, GEN, HNGE, MSFT, NET, RNG and TEAM after the season. It has incremental questions on CHKP, COUR, EVCM, FTNT, HUBS, NABL, NOW, PEGA, PLTR, QLYS and TDC.
JFrog rose 35% on revenue growth of 30.9% and a revenue beat of 8.1%, and Cloud revenue grew 60% y/y. RBC calls FROG its favorite midcap growth idea and raised its PT to $121 from $118.

ServiceNow fell 27% despite beating guidance because buyside expectations were higher. Management guided 18% FY/27 subscription growth including a 100bps headwind from AI delivery services bundling. RBC lowered its PT to $165 from $176 and sees 20%+ as possible.

Datadog fell 14% because Q4 revenue was guided slightly below Q3. Management assumes OpenAI consumes at the floor of its commitment, and some early renewals give better unit pricing. RBC would buy on weakness and cut its PT to $270 from $320 on multiple compression.
Fortinet fell 20% on a smaller billings beat, a service revenue miss and lower service revenue guidance. RBC cut its PT to $165 from $205 and expects the stock to be range-bound until CY/27 guidance.
Atlassian fell 16% on a smaller cloud revenue beat and a smaller FY raise than expected. RBC calls the quarter solid, says T+1 reactions seem excessive, and would be buyers on weakness.

Palantir revenue grew 96% y/y and beat consensus by 5.9%, but total RDV grew only 2% q/q, RPO was flat sequentially and Sovereign AI contract durations were shorter than usual. RBC rates the stock Underperform.
Microsoft's Azure growth accelerated 5 points q/q to 48% in constant currency, with lighter than expected capex. Shares rose about 3% after hours.

Pending deals: Schneider Electric is acquiring PTC for $205/share all cash, and Proofpoint is acquiring Varonis for $49.75/share all cash. Five9 agreed to buy Level AI and Dropbox to buy Tigris. Gen Digital said it is not working on a transformative acquisition.

Ad-tech was strong on political spend, CTV and AI optimization. MGNI, LFTO, APP and UNITY rose, while TTD's revenue (down 0.5% y/y) included a roughly 3-point nonrecurring partner benefit, and PUBM fell 11% despite a beat.

Search-dependent and legacy franchises remain pressured. Ziff Davis organic search referrals fell about 37% y/y, EverCommerce saw softer search-driven customer acquisition, and Thryv cut CY/26 guidance.
Cyber was mixed. CHKP missed on firewall refresh and billings, QLYS guided Q4 billings to +8% and fell 14%, and FTNT and FFIV sold off despite beats. TENB and Rapid7 rose 6% and 3%.

earnings_insights: 55 on-quarter software companies reported Q3/26 revenue 2.5% above consensus on average (reported results vs consensus, FX adjusted). Q2/26 was 2.6% and the off-quarter cohort's Q2/26 beat was 2.1%.

Mean profitability beat was 23.0% vs consensus (EPS, adj-EBITDA, OI or FCF depending on the company). Q4/26 revenue guidance was 1.0% above consensus, while Q4/26 profitability guidance was about 14% below.
CY/26 guidance vs consensus: revenue up 1.2% on average and profitability up 4.8% on average.
JFrog Q3/26: revenue growth of +30.9% vs +28.8% q/q, outperformance of 8.1% vs 5.3% q/q, Cloud revenue $101.5M (+60% y/y), RPO $812M (+60% y/y). Q4/26 guide implies +26.6% growth.
AppLovin Q3/26 reported revenue $2.18B (+55%), 5.3% above consensus, adj-EBITDA $1.84B (84% margin).
Liftoff Mobile Q3/26 reported revenue $237M vs consensus $221.7M. Q4 guide raised 6.1% above consensus, with FY/26 guide now at 33% growth and 60% margin.
Palantir 3Q reported revenue $2,313M (+96% y/y), 5.9% above consensus. Adj. operating margin 61.7% vs consensus 60.2%, adj. EPS $0.44 vs consensus $0.41.
Fortinet Q3/26 reported revenue/EPS $2,078M/$0.91 vs consensus $2,064M/$0.66. Billings growth +29% vs consensus +27.5%, and the billings beat was +1.2% vs +11.0% last quarter.
Cadence Q3/26 reported revenue/EPS $1,633.3M/$2.11 vs consensus $1,612.9M/$2.05. Q4/26 guide $1,710.0M/$2.22 vs consensus $1,649.0M/$2.03.
Unity Q3/26 reported revenue/EBITDA $622.1M/$256.6M vs consensus $567.0M/$186.9M. Q4/26 guide $687.0M/$292.5M vs consensus $600.6M/$205.8M.
BILL Holdings Q1/27 reported revenue/EPS $353.8M/$0.96 vs consensus $438.6M/$0.98. FY/27 guide $1,448.5M/$4.07 vs consensus $1,830.4M/$3.77 (revenue lower, EPS higher).
Qualys Q3/26 reported revenue/EPS $188.0M/$2.12 vs consensus $186.6M/$1.96. Revenue upside was 0.7% vs 2.0% last quarter and Q4/26 billings was guided to +8%.
Datadog Q3/26 beat across the board, but the Q4 revenue guide was slightly below Q3 as management assumes OpenAI consumes at the floor of its commitment.
Dynatrace Q2/27 was essentially in line with small constant-currency beats. Constant-currency ARR was in line and organic FY/27 ARR expectations were maintained.
ServiceNow Q3/26 beat guidance across the board. Management triangulated to 18% FY/27 subscription revenue growth including a 100bps headwind, vs RBC's view that 20%+ is possible.
Twilio Q3/26 revenue grew 20% y/y (16% organic), with non-GAAP EPS $1.65 and FCF $369.6M, all above consensus. Q4 and FY27 guidance were ahead of consensus.
Microsoft F1Q: Azure grew 48% in constant currency, up 5 points q/q, and results were ahead of expectations across the board.
IBM Q3/26: software grew 9% in constant currency and outperformed consensus by $140M, infrastructure outperformed by $150M. Revenue guidance maintained at 4-5% and FCF growth raised to over $1B.
Trade Desk Q3 reported revenue $736M (down 0.5% y/y) vs guidance of at least $650M, and adj-EBITDA $266M vs the $160M guide, including about 3 points of nonrecurring partner benefit.
PubMatic Q3/26 reported revenue $79.6M (+17% y/y, about 11% excluding political) vs consensus $76M, and adj. EBITDA $26.0M vs consensus $18.1M.
Magnite Q3/26 CTV revenue grew 39% to $105M vs consensus $99M, now 53% of the business.

risk_factors: AI spending crowding out other software budgets or delaying deal decisions, with slippage noted at DT, HUBS, NOW and TEAM.

charts_described: Exhibit 1 shows average Q3/26 revenue beats by subsector: Ad-Tech 6.7%, Vertical 3.1%, Observability 3.3%, Back Office 2.2%, Infrastructure 2.1%, Security 1.8%, Front Office 1.4%, SaaS 1.2%, all 2.5%.
Exhibit 1 shows Q3/26 profitability beats of 42.5% for Security and 34.4% for Vertical, and day-one price moves of +13.8% for Ad-Tech and -14.6% for Observability.

Exhibit 2 shows quarterly average revenue beats in 2026 of 2.4% (Q1), 2.6% (Q2) and 2.5% (Q3) vs 2.9%, 3.1% and 2.8% in 2025, and ARR/billings beats of 2.1%, 3.4% and 1.5% in 2026 vs 1.2%, 2.9% and 1.6% in 2025.
vol_and_positioning: Q3 post-print moves were more volatile to the downside than Q2. FROG, APP, LFTO, MGNI and PCOR rose more than 20%, while FFIV, FTNT, COUR, FSLY, NOW and APPS fell more than 20%.

Average day-one move across 55 on-quarter names was -2.3%, and -2.1% from the report date to the 11/13 close. Observability averaged -14.6% on day one and -17.5% through 11/13, while Ad-Tech averaged +13.8% and +15.4%.
Large day-one drops often extended after hours or came despite beats, including NOW -27%, FSLY -27%, COUR -26%, FFIV -20% and FTNT -20%, which RBC attributes to elevated buyside expectations.
Investor sentiment going into Q3 was positive after a solid run from Q2 across cyber, data and infra. RBC says a reversion to crowding into tier 1 AI names is possible.

tension_points.bull_case: Tier 1 AI winners such as NET, DDOG and NOW have durable AI monetization, and recent selloffs leave off-quarter tier 1 names with attractive valuations and expected beat and raises. AI monetization is becoming real and AI ARR is growing at RNG and others.
tension_points.bear_case: AI is crowding out other software budgets and elongating deal cycles. Tier 2 beneficiaries disappointed, beats and billings are the weakest since Q1/25, and patience for AI metrics not visible in top-line results is thin.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Off-quarter tier 1 names such as PANW failing to deliver the expected beat and raises, or the typical Q4 budget flush failing to appear.

tension_points.bull_case: Forward AI ACV commentary was positive and RBC thinks 20%+ FY/27 subscription growth is possible vs management's 18%, with the stock at 6.8x CY/28E EV/S and 18.8x CY/28E FCF.
tension_points.bear_case: Until AI ACV shows up in cRPO and subscription revenue and guidance, investors are likely to remain skeptical and the 18% FY/27 guide can read as disappointing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI ACV failing to show up in cRPO and subscription revenue and guidance.
